newsitem.title: USA: Van Damme's 'Maximum Risk' opens at top of U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: Van Damme's 'Maximum Risk' opens at top of U.S. box office.

text.p: "Maximum Risk", the latest movie from Belgian action hero Jean-Claude Van Damme, opened at the top of the U.S. box office with an estimated weekend gross of $5.8 million.

Once again, there were few marquee titles in the traditionally limp period following the Labor Day holiday weekend as the studios readied their fall lineup of Oscar contenders, such as "Michael Collins" and "Portrait of a Lady".
In "Maximum Risk", Van Damme plays a French cop who assumes the identity of the dead twin brother he never knew existed. It played on 2,358 screens and generated a screen average of just $2,460.
The movie is released by Columbia Pictures, a unit of Sony Corp., which also had the number two movie, "Fly Away Home", starring Academy Award-winner Anna Paquin.
"Fly Away Home" opened with $5.0 million from 1,300 screens, and its average of $3,846 was the highest in the top 10. Paquin plays a young girl who leads a flock of geese to safety.

Last week's number one, the Damon Wayans-Adam Sandler movie, "Bulletproof", fell to third with $4.0 million. The movie is released by Universal Pictures, a unit of Seagram Co. Ltd. Its 10-day gross is $11.8 million.
"Tin Cup" and "First Kid" each slipped two places to fourth and fifth respectively. "Tin Cup", released by Time Warner Inc.'s Warner Bros., earned $3.5 million for a gross to date of $46.8 million.
Walt Disney Co.'s "First Kid" earned an estimated $3.3 million for a 17-day total of $17.7 million.

Among movies in limited or moderate release, the new Keanu Reeves movie, "Feeling Minnesota", opened in 11th with $1.7 million from 869 screens for an average of $1,956. The movie is released by Fine Line Features, a unit of Turner Broadcasting System Inc.

"Grace of My Heart", which is lossely based on the life of singer-songwriter Carole King, earned $168,700 from 45 screens for a stellar average of $3,749. The movie is released by Gramercy Pictures, a unit of PoloyGram NV.

"American Buffalo", a big screen version of the David Mamet play starring Dustin Hoffman and Dennis Franz, earned $153,000 from 29 screens for an average of $5,276. The movie is released by Orion Pictures, a unit of Metromedia International Group Inc.
